newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmen 1997 natural gas output seen at 44 bcm.
newsitem.headline: Turkmen 1997 natural gas output seen at 44 bcm.

text.p: Turkmenistan's production of natural gas for 1997 is seen at 44 billion cubic metres (bcm), the official Turkmen-Press news agency said on Monday.
The agency said the former Soviet republic produced around 35 bcm in 1996, way below 1993 production of 63.5 bcm.

Earlier this month Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov said the largely desert nation of 3.8 million would nearly double exports of natural gas in 1997 to 40 bcm, half of which is earmarked for consumers in western Europe.
The agency said Turkmenistan would earn around $1.5 billion in revenues from gas exports in 1997.
Output of natural gas fell sharply in the energy-rich republic after Russia stopped Turkmen gas from reaching western markets through its pipeline network from 1993.
Niyazov said this month Russia's RAO Gazprom had agreed once more to export Turkmen gas through its pipelines.
